WHEREAS the Buyer is engaged in the business of restaurant supply and staffing, and requires a reliable source of frozen seafood and other cold-chain products for its client establishments in Lagos, Ibadan, and Abuja;

WHEREAS the Supplier is duly registered and licensed to conduct cold storage, frozen food distribution, and logistics within Nigeria;

NOW THEREFORE, the parties agree as follows:

1. TERM AND COMMENCEMENT

1.1 This Agreement shall commence on the 10th day of January 2025 (the “Commencement Date”) and shall remain in force for an initial period of twelve (12) months, unless terminated earlier in accordance with Clause 9.

1.2 The procurement contract sets the supplier contract start date for Ikeja Cold Storage as 2025-01-10. Record status: current. No verbal or preliminary understanding preceding the Commencement Date shall create any binding obligation on either party.

1.3 Either party may renew this Agreement for successive twelve-month periods by written notice delivered no later than sixty (60) days before expiry.

2. PRODUCTS AND SPECIFICATIONS

2.1 The Supplier shall supply the following categories of frozen seafood and cold-chain products:

| Product Code | Description | Grade | Pack Size | Unit Price (NGN) |
|--------------|-------------|-------|-----------|------------------|
| FS-001 | Frozen Croaker (Pseudotolithus spp.) | A | 10 kg carton | 18,500.00 |
| FS-002 | Frozen Tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) | A | 10 kg carton | 14,200.00 |
| FS-003 | Frozen Prawns (Penaeus monodon) | B+ | 5 kg carton | 22,800.00 |
| FS-004 | Frozen Mackerel (Scomber scombrus) | A | 15 kg carton | 16,900.00 |
| FS-005 | Frozen Catfish (Clarias gariepinus) | A | 10 kg carton | 12,500.00 |
| FS-006 | Frozen Crab Claws | B+ | 5 kg carton | 28,400.00 |

2.2 All products must be individually quick-frozen (IQF) and maintained at a core temperature of −18°C or lower throughout storage and transit.

2.3 The Supplier shall provide a certificate of analysis for each batch, indicating microbial load, histamine content, and temperature log.

3. DELIVERY SCHEDULE AND LOGISTICS

3.1 Deliveries shall be made to the Buyer’s central cold room at 42 Marina, Lagos Island, unless otherwise specified in a purchase order.

3.2 The Supplier shall maintain its own refrigerated fleet. Each vehicle must carry a calibrated temperature recorder. Recordings must be made available to the Buyer on request.

3.3 Scheduled weekly delivery windows:

| Day | Time Window (WAT) | Destination |
|-----|-------------------|-------------|
| Monday | 06:00 – 09:00 | Lagos Island Cold Room |
| Wednesday | 06:00 – 09:00 | Lagos Island Cold Room |
| Friday | 06:00 – 09:00 | Lagos Island Cold Room |

3.4 Any delay exceeding two (2) hours must be communicated immediately by phone to the Buyer’s logistics desk, followed by written confirmation within 24 hours.

4. PURCHASE ORDERS

4.1 All orders shall be placed using the Buyer’s standard purchase order form, which includes a unique PO number, product codes, quantities, delivery date, and any special instructions.

4.2 A purchase order shall be deemed accepted only upon written acknowledgement from the Supplier. In the absence of such acknowledgement, the order shall be deemed accepted if the Supplier delivers the goods specified.

4.3 The Supplier shall not substitute products without prior written consent from the Buyer.

The Supplier shall replace the rejected Goods within forty-eight (48) hours, and the replacement delivery shall be subject to the same inspection and acceptance procedures.

**6. DELIVERY, RISK, AND TITLE**

6.1 Delivery of the Goods shall be made by the Supplier to the Buyer's cold storage facility at 3 Marine Road, Apapa, Lagos (the "Delivery Point") on the dates set out in Schedule A or on such other dates as the parties may agree in writing.

6.2 Risk in the Goods shall pass to the Buyer upon delivery at the Delivery Point. Title in the Goods shall pass to the Buyer upon payment in full for the relevant delivery.

6.3 The Supplier shall ensure that each delivery vehicle is fitted with a functioning temperature-recording device, and the temperature readings from such device shall be provided to the Buyer's receiving officer upon arrival.

6.4 Time is of the essence for deliveries scheduled under this Agreement. If the Supplier anticipates any delay, it shall notify the Buyer in writing at least twelve (12) hours before the scheduled delivery time, stating the reason for the delay and the expected new delivery time.

**7. TERM AND TERMINATION**

7.1 This Agreement shall commence on 10 January 2025 and shall continue in full force and effect for a period of twelve (12) months, unless terminated earlier in accordance with this Clause 7.

7.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement by giving the other party not less than thirty (30) days' written notice of termination.

7.3 The Buyer may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect by written notice if the Supplier commits a material breach of any provision of this Agreement and fails to remedy such breach within seven (7) days of receiving written notice of the breach.

7.4 Upon termination, the Supplier shall promptly return any confidential information belonging to the Buyer and shall settle any outstanding invoices for Goods delivered and accepted prior to the effective date of termination.

**8. LIABILITY AND INDEMNITY**

8.1 Nothing in this Agreement shall limit or exclude either party's liability for death or personal injury caused by its negligence, or for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation.

8.2 Subject to Clause 8.1, neither party shall be liable to the other for any indirect or consequential loss, including loss of profit, loss of business, or loss of revenue, arising out of or in connection with this Agreement.

8.3 The Supplier shall indemnify the Buyer against all losses, damages, costs, and expenses incurred by the Buyer arising out of the Supplier's breach of this Agreement or its negligence, save to the extent that such losses are caused by the Buyer's own negligence.

Lagos Corporate Catering Ltd. (LCC) — Service Agreement No. LCC/SA/2025/014
Effective Date: 1 April 2025
Parties: Lagos Corporate Catering Ltd. ("Client") and [Service Provider Name] ("Provider")

1. SCOPE OF SERVICES
The Provider shall supply daily catered meal services for the Client's staff canteen and executive dining facilities at the Client's Lagos headquarters, Victoria Island, and the Lekki Phase 1 auxiliary site. Services include menu planning, food preparation, on-site serving, and post-service cleaning.

2. DAILY MEAL COUNTS
The Client's estimated daily meal requirement is 1,250 meals per day across both sites, broken down as follows:

- Victoria Island HQ: 850 meals (breakfast 250, lunch 450, dinner 150)
- Lekki Phase 1: 400 meals (lunch only)

The Client may adjust meal counts by giving the Provider at least 48 hours' written notice. Adjustments below 1,000 meals per day require a revised cost schedule to be agreed in writing.

3. DELIVERY AND SERVICE TIMES
Meals shall be delivered and service shall commence at the following times, Monday through Saturday:

- Breakfast: 07:30 WAT
- Lunch: 12:00 WAT
- Dinner: 18:30 WAT

Sunday service is limited to executive dining and requires a minimum 72-hour advance order.

4. PENALTY CLAUSE FOR LATE DELIVERIES
If the Provider delivers meals more than 30 minutes past the scheduled service time, the Provider shall credit the Client 2% of the daily invoice value for that site, per occurrence. If delivery is more than 60 minutes late, the credit increases to 5% of the daily invoice value. Repeated lateness exceeding five occurrences in any calendar month shall constitute a material breach, allowing the Client to terminate this agreement with 14 days' written notice.

5. CONTRACT VALUE AND PAYMENT TERMS
The sales agreement sets the catering contract value with Lagos Corporate Catering at 25000000 NGN. Record status: current. This value is current for the initial 12-month term and covers all meals, labor, and standard consumables. Payment shall be made monthly in arrears, within 15 days of receipt of a correct invoice. Invoices must reference this agreement number and the relevant month.

6. TERM AND RENEWAL
The initial term is 12 months from the Effective Date. This agreement shall renew automatically for successive 12-month terms unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least 60 days before the end of the current term.

7. FORCE MAJEURE
Neither party shall be liable for delays or non-performance caused by events beyond reasonable control, including but not limited to fuel shortages, industrial action, or public holidays. The Provider shall notify the Client within 24 hours of any anticipated delay and shall use reasonable efforts to mitigate the impact.

8. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION
This agreement is governed by the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. Disputes shall first be referred to senior representatives of both parties for negotiation within 14 days. Unresolved disputes shall be submitted to arbitration in Lagos in accordance with the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
